source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Compost/organic fertilizer: organic compost can be applied at a rate of roughly 10-20 tons per hectare, adjusting according to the field's existing soil fertility.

Organic sources with known nutrient content: compost/manure can supply approximately N (nitrogen) 217 kg/ha, P (phosphorus) 156 kg/ha, and K (potassium) 158 kg/ha.

Where chemical fertilizer alone is used for nutrient value: N about 264 kg/ha, P about 240 kg/ha, and K about 200 kg/ha.

Recommended fertilizer mix ratio: for basal application (before/at sowing), the source recommends N:P:K roughly at 5% : 100% : 100% of the total nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium requirement respectively -- i.e. essentially all phosphorus and potassium is applied at planting, while only a small share of nitrogen is applied basally.

Nitrogen top-dressing schedule: the remaining nitrogen is applied in split top-dressings -- split 1: 25% of nitrogen, applied 20-25 days after planting; split 2: 25% of nitrogen, applied 40-45 days after planting.

Numeric discrepancy flagged: the source states the basal nitrogen share is 5% and that the 'remaining' 95% is then covered by the two 25% top-dressings, but 5% + 25% + 25% sums to only 55%, not 100%. This gap (about 45% of the nitrogen requirement) is not accounted for elsewhere in the legible text -- it may reflect a missing third top-dressing or a source/OCR error, and is reported here as-is rather than resolved by guessing.

Specific NPK compound fertilizer recommendations given in the source:
- Before sowing (basal, into the furrow/hole): NPK 20-20-15+TE at about 190 kg/ha, or alternatively NPK 16-16-8-13S at about 200 kg/ha.
- Top-dressing when corn has 6-8 leaves: NPK 16-8-16 or NPK 15-15-15 at about 200 kg/ha.
- Top-dressing when corn has 10-12 leaves (before flowering): NPK 16-8-16 or NPK 15-15-15 at about 190 kg/ha.

Application technique: fertilizer should be placed near the root zone at a depth of about 10-15 cm so it does not directly touch and burn the young roots or seed; fertilizer should not be allowed to touch the seed directly at sowing time, as this can damage germination.
